texts.facts: This Interim Application has been filed seeking intervention in the pending Suo Motu Public Interest Litigation No.3 of 2023. The applicant- bakeries are seeking setting aside/withdrawal of the notice dated 29 th January 2025 issued by the Medical Officer of Health, E Ward, Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai. An alternative prayer has been made for a direction upon the respondent-Authority not to enforce the notice dated 29th January 2025. The applicant-bakeries have also made a prayer for extension of the time by one year for transition of the bakeries from conventional fuel to cleaner fuel regime so as to comply the directions issued by the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai vide its notice dated 29th January 2025. 2. Twelve bakeries have approached the Court through this Interim Application. The applicant-bakeries state that there are about 750 bakeries in the City of Mumbai and about 2000 bakeries in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. These bakeries have long and rich cultural history dating back beyond a century and these are largely family-run business. They have given a description of the produces from their bakeries and stated that these products are the only source of food to the citizens and their business provides dignified employment to thousands of unskilled and semi-skilled laborers. In this Interim Application, the applicant-bakeries have referred to the notices issued to them whereby they have been intimated the timeline for switching over to gas/electrical fuel source. In connection therewith, B.D.Pandit-SPS 3 913- IA-9522-25 bakeries.doc they have also referred to the Circular dated 22 nd November 2024. After reproducing the relevant extracts from Faiz Alam Bakery, Masoodul Hasn Khan And ... vs High Court Of Judicature At Bombay On Its ... on 21 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8625011/ 2 the order dated 9 th January 2015 passed by this Court in Suo Motu Public Interest Litigation No.3 of 2023, these applicant-bakeries have endeavored to demonstrate that the order dated 9th January 2025 was passed in breach of natural justice and discriminates them among the small Enterprises. The applicants have further stated that the implication of the order dated 9th January 2025 would have a far reaching effect and would cause hardship to the public at large. 3. An affidavit dated 21st August 2025 sworn on behalf of the Applicant No.9 (Indian Bakery) has been tendered in the Court. In this affidavit, the Applicant No. 9 states as under :- 5. The wood-fired oven in my bakery occupies an area of approximately 180 sq. ft. (12 ft x 15 ft). While my bakery operates only one oven, most bakeries operate two such ovens, made of brick and stone and permanently embedded into the structure Transitioning to PNG ovens requires complete demolition of these wood-fired ovens and installation of new PNG-compatible structures. This is a complex and time-consuming process and will entail a shutdown of the oven while this is underway. Based on industry quotations and consultations, this change will take at least two months and cost between Rs 15-20 lakhs, including demolition, civil work, equipment purchase, safety upgrades, and gas fitting. These are major changes, which can only be commenced once there is assurance of a reliable PNG supply. An abrupt shutdown of bakeries without workable alternatives will disrupt supply chains, affect consumers, and cause unnecessary hardship to the poor. This includes persons engaged in and dependent on the trade and/or persons who depend on pav as an affordable food item. 6. I have set out in paragraph 10 below, why LPG as a fuel is not feasible, practical, viable or safe. The authorities concerned have recognised this and have therefore themselves contemplated a switch to PNG. 7. All the Applicants herein have already made applications to Mahanagar Gas Limited ("MGL"), the only authorised PNG distributor for new connections.
texts.arguments: Upon inquiries about the status of our applications, we have been informed that PNG pipelines have to be laid onto the roads, for connectivity and supply to our area. This will probably be available by mid - 2026, subject to permission from the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai ("MCGM") to undertake B.D.Pandit-SPS 4 913- IA-9522-25 bakeries.doc road digging and laying of pipelines. MGL has also orally clarified that this process can only commence after the monsoon season, creating further unavoidable delays. In these circumstances, initiating reconstruction of ovens without certainty of supply would be counterproductive, economically burdensome, and leave the bakery inoperable. 8. The use of PNG ovens also requires upgrading the sanctioned electricity load. Even though electricity is not needed as a heat generator, PNG ovens are more complex than wood fired ovens, since gas is capable of rapid disposal and requires several additional features such as an ignition system, safety cut-off valves, exhaust and temperature control system. These safety and automation systems operate on electricity and consume a higher load than wood-fired ovens. The enhancement Faiz Alam Bakery, Masoodul Hasn Khan And ... vs High Court Of Judicature At Bombay On Its ... on 21 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8625011/ 3 of electricity load involves applications, assessments, and infrastructure changes through the local electricity distribution company, which further adds to the timeline and complexity. 9. Electric ovens are not a viable alternative due to their high operational costs. The capital cost of setting up a comparable electrically operated oven would be significantly higher than that of a PNG oven. To the best of my knowledge, no bakery of comparable size and scale in Mumbai currently uses electricity as a primary fuel source for baking." 4. In his affidavit, Applicant No.9 states that he is committed to transition of PNG Ovens as soon as supply of PNG becomes available and undertakes to fully cooperate with the Authorities for inspection and compliance requirements. 5. Mr. Venkatesh Dhond, the learned senior counsel for the applicant- bakeries submits that the applicant-bakeries were not made parties and not heard before the order dated 9th January 2025 came to be passed. It is submitted that the applicant-bakeries are required to demolish existing buildings and invest huge money for shifting to alternative fuel source and it would take some time to switch over to clean fuel source. The learned senior counsel submits that much before the order dated 9 th January 2025 was passed, many of the bakeries had been in correspondence with the Mahanagar Gas Limited (in short, MGL) for providing PNG connections. The learned senior counsel tendered copies of e-mails in course of the hearing when this matter was taken up after the recess to apprise the Court B.D.Pandit-SPS 5 913- IA-9522-25 bakeries.doc that one Pahelvi Bakery was, in fact, given clearance by the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board and the MGL for PNG supply. The learned senior counsel has also taken us through the correspondences by the Joint Committee of India Bakers Association and a proposal from the Government for incentive to the Industries which switches over to clean and green energy system. In sum and substance, this is the stand taken by the applicant-bakeries that they have been making bona-fide endeavors but for a confirm commitment to supply PNG by the MGL and other logistics difficulties they are unable to shift to green fuel regime and, therefore, are constrained to approach this Court seeking extension of time by one year. 6. Mr. Darius Khambata, the learned amicus curiae has taken us through the observations made by this Court in its order dated 9 th January 2025 and submitted that the issue of shifting to the green alternative fuel system by the bakeries was discussed by this Court and, after having noticed the previous notices issued and the adverse environmental impact due to coal and wood burning, a timeline has been set for switching over to the alternative energy source. The learned amicus curiae referred to paragraph no. 14 and 15 of the said order wherein this Court observed that effective and immediate steps are required to be taken to control air pollution by the hotels and bakeries. The learned amicus curiae would contend that the applicant-bakeries have no right in law under Article 19(g) of the Constitution of India to carry on business through a polluting establishment and the right of the citizens under Article 21 of the Constitution of India must prevail over the individual rights of the applicant-bakeries even though some hardship is caused to them. 7. Insofar as the pollution created by Hotels, Bakeries and Bhattis etc., is concerned, the same is caused as these units use either wood or coal. The learned counsel appearing for the MGL stated that on site B.D.Pandit-SPS 8 913- IA-9522-25 bakeries.doc inspection it was observed that it is not feasible to provide PNG supply to the applicant-bakeries. Though the learned senior counsel for the applicant- bakeries took objection on the ground that no such statement has been made on oath, we are not inclined to ask the respondents to file their affidavit-in-opposition to this Interim Application. It would take precedence over unemployment, business prospects and other factors of similar nature. Faiz Alam Bakery, Masoodul Hasn Khan And ... vs High Court Of Judicature At Bombay On Its ... The learned senior counsel for the applicant-bakeries lastly submitted that a specific prayer under prayer clause (e) of the Interim Application has been made seeking extension of time by one year and the applicants are ready and willing to comply with the Court's order provided they are given PNG connections.
